item.title: Zuiganji Temple: Tohoku's Great Zen Temple — Guide
item.description: Zuiganji is Tohoku’s most important Zen temple, founded in 828 and rebuilt in its current magnificent form by Date Masamune in 1609 — the gilded sliding-door paintings inside the main hall are among the finest surviving examples of Momoyama-period art. The approach from the main gate is one of Japan’s most atmospheric temple walks: a corridor of ancient cedar trees several hundred years old, their canopy blotting out the sky, lined with cliff-carved meditation caves.
